# ADR-0072: Stabilize the current kit and resume improvements on demand

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Type:** strategy
- **Date:** 2026-09-17
- **Partly supersedes:** ADR-0069's immediate starter-completion work order only
- **Extends:** ADR-0019, ADR-0045 and ADR-0066

## Context

The owner reports excessive usage with little movement in weighted completion and
explicitly prioritizes responsible landing over finishing every remaining quality
experiment now. Useful implementations and bounded accepted outcomes already exist;
unresolved acceptance, research and distribution work are not all shipping blockers.
The large shared dirty worktree also prevents an indiscriminate completion commit.

## Decision

End the open-ended G1–G6 execution campaign after a bounded stabilization handoff.
Keep the vision, original acceptance criteria and evidence. G2/G5's accepted bounded
outcomes remain accepted; G1/G3/G4/G6 residuals become demand-triggered, not completed.
No automatic full-catalog certification, browser matrix, consumer migration or new
feature is required to close this handoff. Fix a demonstrated immediate regression
in the supported path or isolate it; promotion-only research may remain parked.

The canonical [resumption guide](../design/stabilization-and-resumption.md) owns task
packets, triggers and stop rules. Scope owns campaign priority; the existing CUE
inventory owns component requirements/readiness, and dated receipts own observations.
Use the existing MCP document route and ordinary Fathom index. Do not add or compile
a semantic layer without a measured retrieval gap and separately bounded evaluation.

Every resumed task selects a named consumer need or an explicit owner-funded
maintenance batch, exact inputs, acceptance, budget and stopping condition before
execution. Reuse prior evidence after checking identity; do not repeat experiments
without a hypothesis whose result changes the next decision. Exhausting the budget
produces a handoff, not automatic expansion or a weaker oracle.

The owner selects a prospective, versioned theme-guide memory contract that bounds
app-owned growth and reports total browser cost. Metric attribution, numerical
thresholds and independent controls must be defined before execution. Existing v1
budgets and failed results remain unchanged; the replacement is not implemented here.
The authorized Fathom guide is deferred by this later priority, not canceled or built.

Preserve unrelated edits, consumer work and failed receipts. Working-tree durability
is not a release: review exact source closure before isolated commits, private pin
delivery or promotion. This decision grants no publishing, deployment, global config,
signing, installation or new cross-repo authority.

## Alternatives and consequences

- Finish every original gate now: rejected as an unbounded current work order.
- Declare completion by shrinking the denominator: rejected; report accepted,
  partial, failed and deferred separately, with no artificial percentage increase.
- Add another status database or compiled policy layer: unnecessary maintenance now.
- Demand-led work accepts unfinished optional capabilities while preserving the
  standards and exact steps needed when a real adopter requires them.

## Revisit when

- A named adopter needs a parked task or encounters a reproducible supported-path bug.
- The owner funds a bounded maintenance batch with explicit acceptance and stop limits.
- Resume guidance loses a necessary dependency, receipt or authority boundary.
- Measured retrieval failures justify evaluating an additional semantic route.
